name: Kurdish nationalism
summary: Kurdish nationalism holds that the Kurds are a single nation with a right to govern themselves, divided between Turkey, Iraq, Iran and Syria by the post-First World War settlement. Its demands range from cultural and language rights and regional autonomy to an independent, unified Kurdistan. It says little about economics or social policy, and its parties range from the conservative, secular and market-leaning KDP to leftist and Islamic currents.
scope: The mainstream pan-Kurdish national movement from Sheikh Ubeydullah's 1880 revolt and the post-1918 Sevres-era claims through the KDP/PUK-led autonomy struggle in Iraq and the 2017 independence referendum. It excludes the PKK-style democratic confederalist strand, which rejects the nation-state, and the Kurdish-Islamic strand. Most economic and social answers are low-confidence inferences.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Mainstream Kurdish parties never made health policy a defining issue; the KRG provides public clinics, so mild support is inferred from the regional governments' practice.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Kurdish nationalism has no wage doctrine; adherents range from the market-oriented KDP to leftist currents, so the strand is genuinely split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The KDP is listed as economically liberal while the PKK-linked left rejects capitalism, so adherents are split and the nationalism itself is indifferent.

public-ownership.rationale: Kurdish regional governments treat oil as a public resource contested with Baghdad, but nationalists are split between liberal and leftist economics.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No nationalist doctrine on taxation exists; the KDP's economic liberalism and the left's redistribution pull opposite ways.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are not a nationalist theme; the 1946 KDP programme deliberately avoided social and economic commitments to keep landlords and chiefs onside.

property-fundamental.rationale: The founding KDP programme avoided economic commitments to keep landlords on board, and later economic liberalism sits beside leftist currents, leaving no settled line.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Economic regulation was never central to the national movement and the main parties diverge on it, so no stance is stated.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not an issue the movement addressed; the Kurdistan Region runs large public payrolls, but nationalists are not united on welfare.

worker-ownership.rationale: Mainstream KDP and PUK-led governments did not pursue worker ownership; only the leftist fringe of the movement does, so a mild no is inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Kurdish nationalists have both fought terrorism (ISIS) and suffered state surveillance, and no common position is documented.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Nothing in the programmes touches drug policy; the socially conservative mainstream of the KDP suggests mild opposition.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; Kurdish nationalists have suffered censorship of their language, which cuts against speech restrictions, but minority protection cuts the other way.

strong-leader.rationale: Nationalism has produced charismatic leaders (the Barzani family) but also democratic claims; adherents are split on bypassing gridlock.

state-harmful.rationale: Kurdish nationalism seeks a state or autonomous government of its own, so it regards states as necessary and rejects anarchism.

limit-guns.rationale: Peshmerga culture and armed self-defence are tied to national survival, so strict gun limits are unlikely to be favoured; inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: Peshmerga and security forces are central to defending the Kurdish region against Baghdad and ISIS, so strengthening them is favoured.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not a nationalist question; the socially conservative mainstream implies mild opposition.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal philosophy is not addressed by the movement, and no majority line is documented.

traditional-family.rationale: The KDP is described as conservative, implying support for traditional family values, though leftist and women's movements dissent.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The conservative mainstream of Kurdish politics does not support it and the Kurdistan Region does not recognise it; inferred, as it is not a nationalist issue.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not a nationalist question; conservative mainstream parties are likelier to oppose, though women's movements dissent.

more-religion-public.rationale: The KDP lists secularism among its ideologies and the movement is mostly secular, though Kurdish-Islamic strands dissent.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Kurds seek redress for national oppression such as Anfal, but 'racial injustice' in the usual sense is not a nationalist theme; split.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed by nationalist programmes; women's movement currents may agree while conservatives do not.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Defending Kurdish language, culture and identity against assimilation is the core of the movement.

gradual-change.rationale: The movement has repeatedly risen in revolt (1880, 1946, 1961, 1991) rather than waiting, though it also negotiates; mild disagreement.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration is not a nationalist theme; the Kurdistan Region hosts many refugees and displaced people without a settled line.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Kurdish nationalists have appealed to the League of Nations and Western powers for recognition, suggesting mild support for international bodies.

free-trade.rationale: No trade doctrine; the KRG favours foreign investment while nationalists are split on economics.

nation-first.rationale: The movement puts national self-determination ahead of the Iraqi, Turkish, Iranian and Syrian states it lives in, though it courts alliances.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Kurds were protected by the 1991 no-fly zone and Western action against ISIS, so they generally welcome intervention to protect populations.

open-borders.rationale: Kurdish nationalism wants borders for its own territory, and the movement's drive is for states rather than open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: A stateless, resource-rich movement seeking oil revenue has not embraced degrowth; inferred from the oil dispute.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate policy is not a nationalist theme and the movement depends on oil revenue.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No documented position; Kurdish regional politics centres on oil and gas.

revolution-justified.rationale: Armed uprisings against central states are part of the movement's history and the PKK and others claim a right of armed resistance, though the KDP also negotiates.

central-planning.rationale: Centralised planning is not part of the movement and the mainstream KDP is economic liberal; leftist currents dissent.

socialized-markets.rationale: Economic models are not defined by the nationalism, and parties differ.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Kurdistan Region governments have steered oil and investment, but nationalists lack a common doctrine.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Agrarian reform was a point of dispute inside the KDP (Ubayd Allah Barzani criticised his father for not carrying it out), so adherents split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Kurdish nationalism as practised by KDP and PUK is committed to a money economy; only extreme leftists propose abolition.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Nationalism takes no position, and the movement's governments rely on state finance, so mild disagreement is inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not a feature of Kurdish nationalism; inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: The nationalist movement claims democratic legitimacy and runs multi-party elections, although the KDP is accused of authoritarianism.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The movement has been republican since Mahabad (1946) and hereditary leadership by Barzanis is dynastic but not monarchy; Kurdish sheikhs led early revolts though.

democracy-best.rationale: The KRG has multi-party elections and nationalist parties profess democratic values, though some critics say the KDP falls short.

direct-votes.rationale: Kurdish nationalists staged a direct referendum on independence in 2017 and claim self-determination through plebiscite.

workers-councils.rationale: Council-based democracy appears only in the leftist/PKK fringe; mainstream nationalism uses parliaments.

right-to-secede.rationale: Self-determination up to independence is the movement's central claim and the 2017 referendum asserted it.

natural-rulers.rationale: Tribal leadership persists but nationalist programmes claim democratic legitimacy; inferred.

political-violence-never.rationale: Armed struggle by peshmerga and the PKK is celebrated as legitimate resistance, though some strands pursue only political means.

war-builds-character.rationale: Peshmerga heroism is valued, but no doctrine says war builds character.

separate-church-state.rationale: The KDP lists secularism, and the main nationalist movement is secular, though Kurdish-Islamic parties dissent.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The mainstream is secular; only Kurdish Islamist parties favour scripture-based law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The movement wants a state with its own justice and defence forces.

military-superiority.rationale: A stateless movement with a defensive posture has not framed this goal; split.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Kurdish nationalism is ethnic-linguistic in origin, yet the KRG reserves seats for Turkmen, Assyrians, Armenians and claims pluralism, so adherents are split.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The mainstream sees national oppression, not class, as the driver; the PKK left differs.

equal-outcomes.rationale: No stated position and strands differ.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Kurds claim authority over their ancestral Kurdistan, but as a nation more than as an indigenous people; inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Kurds seek redress from regional states rather than colonial powers; the 1920s partition by European powers is resented but reparations are not demanded.

civilizational-union.rationale: Kurdish nationalism asserts a distinct Kurdish nation, not union of Muslims or Arabs; Kurdish-Islamic strands are an exception.

limit-population.rationale: The movement stresses Kurdish numbers and demographic strength, suggesting opposition to limiting population; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not addressed; the movement seeks development and oil wealth.

restore-past-order.rationale: Nationalism is forward-looking in seeking a state, though it invokes lost autonomy; mild disagreement inferred.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Parties pragmatically shift between autonomy and independence, but no formal doctrine exists.

direct-action.rationale: The movement uses both elections and insurgency, so adherents are split.

return-to-foraging.rationale: A movement wanting statehood and development rejects abandoning civilisation.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not part of nationalism and incompatible with state-building.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Leftist currents agree; mainstream nationalists do not. Split.

production-for-use.rationale: Leftist currents agree and liberal ones do not, so split.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The mainstream KDP is economically liberal and does not treat profit as exploitation; leftists differ.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Class dictatorship has no place in a nationalist programme.

collective-farming.rationale: Not part of mainstream nationalism, which sided with landlords and chiefs in the 1946 programme.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not a nationalist thesis; leftist strands accept it.

taxation-theft.rationale: The movement seeks a taxing state; inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Nationalism makes national collective rights central, so it rejects the view that rights belong to individuals only.

conscription.rationale: Peshmerga recruitment and mandatory service have been debated; no clear doctrine.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The movement stresses voice and self-rule within a homeland, not exit; inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Kurdish nationalism defines nationhood by language and shared history; racial hierarchy is not a documented tenet.

organic-representation.rationale: Parties and elections are the nationalist norm; inferred.

total-state.rationale: The movement opposes assimilationist states controlling all culture and does not advocate totalitarian rule.

national-rebirth.rationale: Kurdish nationalism frames a national awakening after repression, though 'decadence' is not the framing.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Claims on Kirkuk and other disputed territories exist, but the aim is unification of Kurdish lands, not general expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Tribal loyalty persists in Kurdish politics, but nationalist programmes claim modern legitimacy.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is contrary to nationalist modernisation and to Barzani-era critiques of landlords.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Kurdish nationalists have often had ties with Israel and Israel backed the 2017 referendum, but this is not a nationalist tenet and Kurdish views vary.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Kurdish nationalists welcome the Kurdish diaspora as part of the nation, which implies support for return; inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: Kurdish language revival and recognition (Kurdish official in Iraq) is central, though Kurdish is already in everyday use.

workplace-democracy.rationale: No documented position; leftist strands favour it.

economic-freedom.rationale: Split between liberal and leftist currents.

rule-by-example.rationale: Nationalist programmes rely on parties and law.

national-self-determination.rationale: Every nation's right to its own state is the central claim; Kurds cite their exclusion from Lausanne and the Sevres promise of independence.

force-without-un.rationale: Kurds benefited from interventions with and without UN authority; no doctrine.

class-collaboration.rationale: The mainstream national movement sought to unite chiefs, landlords and workers under one national banner, as in the 1946 KDP programme.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Defending Kurdish heritage is central, so sacrificing cultural institutions is rejected.

dominated-front.rationale: Kurdish nationalists rely on Western backing, so anti-Western fronts are not favoured, but this is not a stated tenet.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Women have prominent political and military roles, and the KRG has a 30 percent quota; leftist strand strongly dissents, conservatives less so.

ban-interest.rationale: Kurdish-Islamic strands might favour it; the secular mainstream does not.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Kurdish nationalism arose against discrimination, and it champions minority protections in Kurdistan.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Nationalists see states as tools of ethnic domination more than class; only the left applies a class analysis.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Oil and gas are the main economic base of the Kurdistan Region and the dispute with Baghdad concerns exports.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Kurdish nationalists oppose forced assimilation for themselves and the KRG reserves seats for minorities, but this concerns minorities not immigrants; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not part of the movement; Kurds do fear Arabization, but not elite replacement through immigration.

proportional-representation.rationale: The Kurdistan Parliament uses list-proportional voting, though this is not a tenet.

national-mission.rationale: Kurdish nationalism seeks its own self-rule, not to spread a system to others; the Rojava claim is the exception.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Women's movements affirm it and conservative strands do not, so split.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics is alien to the movement.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Kurdish nationalists demand accountability for Anfal, Halabja and Turkish and Syrian abuses.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Kurdish nationalists build state institutions with wide public roles; inferred.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Kurds are a mixed people by their own account; not a nationalist tenet.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Kurdish nationalism is a claim of equal national rights, and the KRG affirms minority rights.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Nationalists describe Arabization settlement in Kirkuk and Syria as colonisation by displacement, though this is not specific to a settler state doctrine.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The KRG protects Yazidi and Christian minorities and the movement is largely religiously plural; inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Secular mainstream, but Islamic parties differ, and policy is unsettled.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Kurdish claims to self-determination rest on popular consent, as in the 2017 referendum and the Sevres mechanism.

population-transfer.rationale: Kurds were victims of forced transfer and Arabization campaigns and the movement opposes them.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Kurdish parties have been banned in Turkey and thus often oppose such bans, but may favour them against rivals.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The idea that being at the mercy of another nation's state is unfree fits the nationalist claim, though not formally stated.

separated-powers.rationale: The Kurdistan system is a parliament with an executive and courts, and the movement seeks democratic checks, though this is not defined.

vanguard-party.rationale: Only the PKK leftist strand has vanguard traditions; mainstream nationalism does not.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The movement ties Kurdish poverty to state neglect and war, not population; inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Kurds fear forced mixing by Arabization yet the KRG touts diversity, so split.

party-controls-media.rationale: Kurdish nationalists have suffered media censorship; the KDP is nonetheless criticised for pressuring media.

party-commands-army.rationale: The KRG's peshmerga are split between KDP and PUK party forces, a practice not endorsed as principle.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Kurdish nationalists aim for their own sovereignty first; federalism within Iraq and Syria is accepted by some, but no stance on supranational unions.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The KRG's semi-presidential disputes (2009 draft constitution) show adherents split.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not applicable to a largely Muslim nation.

clerical-rule.rationale: Secular mainstream rejects clerical rule; only Islamist currents might accept it.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Masoud Barzani's long tenure drew criticism and the 2017 resignation; no doctrine.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The movement has relied on foreign backing from the US and others and is Atlanticist.

people-in-arms.rationale: Peshmerga are volunteer fighters, but nationalists also want a standing army.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not part of the nationalist idea.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The Kurdish identity is rooted in mountains but no doctrine says so.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reuniting Kurds divided among four states by the post-war settlement is the movement's defining aim, though many accept autonomy first.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Nationalists claim equality of Kurdish culture with dominant ones, which implies cultural parity; inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: The Kurdistan Region retains it for terrorism offences, but views differ.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Split between conservative and leftist women's movement strands.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The secular mainstream does not teach it; inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The conservative mainstream is more likely to favour restriction; inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Kurds define the nation by descent and culture, and the diaspora is part of it, but the KRG also admits residents; mild support.

minority-language-support.rationale: Kurdish language rights are core, and the KRG recognises Armenian, Assyrian and Turkmen too.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The mainstream would be satisfied with political independence; leftists want economic change, so split.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The Kurdish parties repeatedly drafted regional constitutions and call for democratic constitution-making, so mild support.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The movement uses democratic claims; inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: A stateless people dependent on allies has not sought one.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The KRG president was directly elected in 2005 and 2009, and the draft constitution disputed whether to retain it.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The Kurdish movement fought over Kirkuk and claims disputed territories, resisting concessions on them.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Kurdish parties differ on how far property should serve the common good, and the nationalism itself sets no rule.

collective-defense.rationale: Kurdish nationalists seek alliance guarantees from Western powers, as with the US-led coalition; inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Kurds view Turkish, Iraqi and Syrian control of Kurdish lands as imposed without their consent, as Sevres envisaged a plebiscite.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Secular mainstream and Islamic parties differ.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Kurdish nationalists have suffered such force (October 2017 recapture of Kirkuk) and reject its legitimacy.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Kurdish regions in Iraq accepted federal autonomy with their own system and law, and the Iranian Kurds mostly seek autonomy.

leader-cult.rationale: Barzani and Ocalan are honoured, yet some Kurdish nationalists oppose cults; split.

land-redistribution.rationale: The KDP programme avoided agrarian reform to keep landlords on side, while its left criticised that.

refugee-return.rationale: Return of Kurds expelled by Arabization and war, notably to Kirkuk and Afrin, is a standard nationalist demand.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Kurdish nationalism claims territory where Kurds live, as in the unified Kurdistan and Kirkuk demands.

women-must-cover.rationale: The mainstream opposes compulsion; Kurdish women prominent in public life including armed forces.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-Kurdish nationalism seeks the political unity of Kurds across borders.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Many Kurdish parties accept autonomy short of a state, especially in Iran and Syria, but others demand independence, so adherents are split.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Kurds mostly stay in their homeland and seek rights there, but also seek a state; split.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Nationalism holds that national identity moves history; only leftists disagree.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The Kurdistan Parliament is required to have at least 30 percent women and the Rojava administration uses co-chairs.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The KRG courts foreign investment and trade.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The PKK's guerrilla strategy does, but the KDP seeks political settlements, so split.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Barzani family leadership and tribal chiefs persist in Kurdish politics; mild rejection inferred from republicanism.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Teaching Kurdish history and language is a central demand.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Kurdish nationalism opposes foreign or Turkish, Arab and Persian rule over Kurds and rejects tutelage.

patriotic-education.rationale: Kurdish language-medium education and national history in schools is a core demand.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Kurds seek independence from the successor states of the Ottoman Empire; Turkish neo-Ottoman influence is opposed.

delink-world-market.rationale: The Kurdistan Region has sought integration into oil markets.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Nationalism arose against discrimination, so it rejects a right to discriminate; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Kurdish draft constitutions and Iraqi federal constitution include rights protection; inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: Kurdish nationalism demands autonomy or federalism against central capitals, as in the Kurdistan Region's residual powers within Iraq.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Kurdish nationalists blame hostile central states for their plight, while critics inside the movement accuse the KDP and PUK elites of enrichment from oil revenue, so adherents are split.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This is a Marxist-Leninist doctrine absent from Kurdish nationalism; mild disagreement is inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Kurdish nationalism accepts armed resistance and peshmerga force, so an absolute non-initiation principle is unlikely to be held; inferred.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Kurdish nationalists have been targets of emergency rule in Turkey and elsewhere, which makes them wary of it.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: No documented position, and liberal and leftist currents differ.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Kurdish nationalists have suffered censorship of their language and culture, and cultural expression is central to the movement.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: No documented position; conservative and leftist currents differ.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Kurdish nationalism treats the post-1918 partition (Sevres replaced by Lausanne) as imposed without Kurdish consent and as the root of its claim.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred from the republican, elected presidency and parliament of the Kurdistan Region; no strand seeks a hereditary throne.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred: the movement seeks majority-rule self-government and has not endorsed individual consent vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the movement's revolts against Ottoman, Iraqi, Iranian and Turkish rule as illegitimate, though the nationalist case rests on national rather than constitutional grounds.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred from the Kurdistan Parliament and the KDP's elected-government model; the issue is not a defining one.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Nationalist programmes do not address animal welfare; mild agreement is inferred from mainstream secular conservatism.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred: mainstream Kurdish parties, pastoral and agricultural in tradition, accept animal use with no strong welfare agenda.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from the KDP's conservative, tribal-leadership tradition, which values patronage and obligation by notables.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: A national movement depends on political mobilisation and participation, so withdrawal runs against its core.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not a theme of Kurdish nationalism, which treats media and culture as tools of national awakening; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The mainstream movement has no theory of class rule; adherents are not split but indifferent.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The mainstream KDP/KRG is market-leaning and courts foreign investment; its economic grievance is against Baghdad over oil, not a world-system. Inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred: the Kurdistan Region's institutions include minority quotas and are not restricted by birth.

party-own-road.rationale: Inferred from the movement's insistence on independent national decision-making rather than direction from other states or parties.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The KRG actively seeks foreign investment, oil contracts and international backing, so reliance on aid and investment is accepted. Inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Claims to Kirkuk and other disputed areas outside the Region are a central demand, central to the 2017 referendum.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Kurds present themselves as indigenous to Kurdistan, but the movement has no settler-versus-native programme; adherents are indifferent.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anti-fascism is not a defining value of the mainstream movement, which is not hostile to it either.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred from the movement's experience of Baathist and other authoritarian rule; no documented stance on the comparison.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The movement has no stake in US history; disagreement is inferred from mainstream scholarship.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred: the movement removes symbols of former oppressors, and builds its own national monuments.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed by the nationalist programme; adherents are indifferent or split.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred: the KRG legislated specifically against violence against women, and the movement stresses women's status.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred: Kurdish parties seek parliamentary democracy on the Western model rather than distinct civilizational forms.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Peshmerga are party forces, but the movement frames them as defending the nation rather than guarding the constitution; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not addressed by the nationalist programme; adherents are indifferent.

filial-duty.rationale: Family respect is common in Kurdish society but is not a nationalist doctrine; inferred from the traditional social outlook of the main parties.

office-by-exam.rationale: The movement has no position on civil-service recruitment; parties use both patronage networks and merit claims.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The movement lacks a doctrine on foreign acquisitions; the KRG actively seeks foreign investment while others worry about control.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not a nationalist issue; the conservative KDP and secular or leftist currents differ.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The KDP and PUK are leader-centred parties that favour representative institutions and did not bind delegates by mandate; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The mainstream parties have no pension doctrine; the KRG runs a public system and the market-leaning KDP is open to private provision.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The mainstream KDP/PUK movement accepts private property, so community tenure of land is contrary; inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The KRG has a parliament that approves its budget and the movement pursues democratic self-government; inferred from the Kurdistan Region's institutions.

single-official-language.rationale: The movement's main language grievance is the suppression of Kurdish by single-language states, and Kurdish and Arabic are both official in Iraq.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The movement has no stated doctrine on foreign land ownership; the KRG has allowed foreign investment but adherents are split.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Kurdish nationalism has no stated view on disparate impact doctrine; adherents are split or indifferent.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The movement has no stance on consumerism; the KRG's market-leaning outlook is offset by traditional criticism of luxury.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Kurdish movements have sought and accepted foreign backing, and Kurdish parties' own insurgent history makes them sympathetic to arming insurgents; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Kurds have been victims of interventions by neighbouring states and want sovereignty respected; inferred from the national-grievance narrative.

corporate-influence.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; the KDP is market-leaning, but adherents are not committed either way.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Kurdish parties seek autonomy rather than foreign isolation and take outside backing, but sovereignty concerns could cut either way; adherents split.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Not a nationalist theme in the sources; a growing population could support the national cause, but this is inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed; no source shows a stance on residency-limited property.

job-guarantee.rationale: The KDP is conservative and market-leaning, so a job guarantee is not part of its program; adherents are split.

democratic-peace.rationale: The movement seeks Western backing and the 2017 referendum appealed to democratic norms, but nothing states a view on democratic peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Kurdish nationalists resist the laws of states that suppressed their language and rights, but they also seek rule of law in their own region; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: The movement asks outside powers for recognition and support of its self-determination, so it does not hold that states may never be intervened against.

industrial-unions.rationale: Not addressed; the KDP is not a labour party and the sources give no stance.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The movement defines the enemy as the states ruling Kurdistan, not a minority conspiracy; inferred, and the sources do not address it.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The KDP stresses a conservative family and does not seek to end legal marriage; inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Kurdistan Region adopted a right-to-information law and its leaders appeal to open government; inferred, not a core theme.

local-production.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; no source shows a position.

informal-organisation.rationale: The KDP and PUK are formal parties with armed wings, not small informal groups; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The movement asks for international recognition and has relied on international guarantees such as Sevres and the referendum, rather than putting national law first.

religious-nation.rationale: Kurdish nationalism is defined by language and ethnicity, and Kurds are of several faiths including Sunni, Yazidi and Alevi, so religion does not define it.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Kurdish nationalism is a demand for recognition of Kurdish self-rule against dominating states, so ritual submission to a leading power is rejected; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The oil-revenue dispute between the KRG and Baghdad is about the region keeping and controlling what it produces, and KRG leaders press for it.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Nationalism has no property doctrine; the KDP is market-leaning while leftist Kurdish currents favour common ownership, so the strand is split.

defeat-communism.rationale: Kurdish parties took varied sides in Cold War alignments, and anti-communism is not a nationalist tenet; the KDP is conservative yet cooperated with the Soviet Union and Iraqi communists at times.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The KDP's economically liberal profile and the KRG's practice of mixing public and private providers imply acceptance; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: Religion is not a core theme; the KDP is secular but adherents include Muslim and traditional communities, and denial that religion endures is a Marxist tenet; inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Nationalism does not address the question of capitalism's historical role; the market-leaning KDP might agree while leftist currents would not.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Kurdish nationalism has no doctrine on the economics of gender equality; the KRG has a women's quota but adherents are split.

socialized-care.rationale: The mainstream, conservative KDP strand favours family and private arrangements for care; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Kurdish nationalism defends Kurdish as a language of schooling and public life rather than purging loanwords, and Kurdish itself is a mix of dialects; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Kurdish nationalists cite Sevres as binding promises that the state broke, so binding commitments are favoured; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The mainstream KDP/PUK strand seeks a state or federal region, not communal property; the PKK-style commune strand is excluded from scope.

majority-settlement.rationale: Kurdish nationalists are the minority in contested regions and oppose Arabisation settlement policies, as in Kirkuk, which they treat as a core grievance.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The mainstream strand is market-leaning, with leftist currents also present, and is not defined by a third-way economics; adherents split.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Kurdish nationalism bases its claim to Kurdistan on the Kurds' long habitation and the Sevres-era recognition of Kurdish areas.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Kurdish nationalism does not deny the Holocaust and compares its own genocide claims to it; inferred, not a stated doctrine.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The KDP-led mainstream is socially conservative but Iraqi Kurdistan has not codified such a ban; inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Kurdish nationalists seek political rights against suppression by their states, though ruling parties have restricted rivals; inferred.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The mainstream movement is secular in outlook; Kurdish-Islamic currents are excluded from scope; inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The movement frames its own situation as domination by the states dividing Kurdistan and is anti-colonial in outlook.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A religious duty outside the secular nationalist mainstream; Kurdish-Islamic strand excluded from scope; inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The KDP-led mainstream is secular and opposes Islamist rule, which scope excludes.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Direct democracy is the PKK strand's creed, which scope excludes; the KDP mainstream favours representative government; split.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: A progressive framework mainly associated with the excluded confederalist strand; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not a concern of the mainstream, which is socially conservative; inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the social conservatism of the mainstream parties.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The movement unites parties from left to right behind a national goal but does not say the division is obsolete.

alienated-labor.rationale: The KDP is market-leaning and conservative, and rejects this Marxian thesis; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Most Kurds are Muslim and the movement does not frame Islam as alien; inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The mainstream is secular and rests authority on the people and referendum, as in 2017; inferred.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: No stated position; adherents are split between secular and conservative views.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: A detail of labour law outside the movement's concerns.

social-market-economy.rationale: KDP's market-leaning outlook alongside public services in the Kurdistan Region suggests mild support; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The movement relies on Peshmerga forces to defend Kurdish autonomy and gives them constitutional standing in Iraq.

rich-first.rationale: No stated view on development strategy.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Kurdish movements have repeatedly sought great-power allies, with the mainstream split between neutrality and alliance; inferred.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Tribal and family leadership is common in the KDP, but the movement has no doctrine on hereditary rule and secular republicans reject it; adherents split.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The KDP is economically liberal and the KRG favours ordinary commercial banks; mutual credit is inferred as unfavoured.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Kurdish nationalism has no doctrine on foreign lenders; the KRG has accepted external fiscal reforms, but sovereignty arguments pull the other way.

property-franchise.rationale: The movement demands self-determination by popular vote, as in the 2017 referendum, which implies universal suffrage; inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: This is the theory of the excluded confederalist strand; mainstream nationalists neither endorse nor oppose it.

reification.rationale: A Marxian critique of markets does not appear in the market-leaning KDP tradition; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Mainstream parties defend formal liberties and a market economy rather than treating them as hollow; inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Kurdish claims rest on treaty and constitutional rights, as in the Sevres articles and the federal Iraq settlement, which implies support for law-bound rule; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: The movement seeks autonomy for Kurds but the Kurdistan Region gives minorities reserved seats and language status, so it does not restrict the vote by ethnicity.

online-participation.rationale: No doctrine on internet participation; inferred as indifferent.

open-government-data.rationale: No doctrine on publishing government records; adherents are indifferent.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The KDP is secular and the region has a tradition of religious pluralism, so a legal limit on interfaith marriage is unlikely to be favoured; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Mainstream Kurdish nationalism courts Christian, Yazidi and other minorities and has no tradition of such boycotts; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Mainstream KDP/PUK nationalism works through elected parliaments, party leadership and referendums such as 2017; sortition is not part of it, so mild disagreement is inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The movement is secular-leaning but includes conservative and religious currents and takes no position on religious reform; adherents are split.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The movement is about self-rule, not wealth distribution; its parties range from market-leaning KDP to leftist currents.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the socially conservative character of mainstream KDP/PUK politics and Kurdistan Region law, which does not recognise open service.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The mainstream movement is secular but does not use the state to promote atheism; inferred from KDP policy and Kurdish religious plurality.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The Kurdistan Region maintains police, Asayish and Peshmerga forces as pillars of self-rule, so abolition is rejected.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from the movement's demand for federalism and the Iraqi constitutional settlement, in which the Kurdistan Region shares power with other communities.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Mainstream Kurdish parties never made this a defining issue; the KRG both funds public programmes and tolerates private charity.

term-limits.rationale: No stated position; KDP leadership has held office long-term, which suggests indifference rather than support.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from the movement's representative parties and referendum process; direct delegation is not part of it.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The movement does not address extinction risk; no principle points either way.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the largely Sunni Muslim and conservative religious institutions in the Kurdistan Region.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from Kurdistan Region legal reforms to family law and the secular character of mainstream Kurdish nationalism.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred; the movement stresses Kurdish national belonging and has no stated position on foreign residents' votes.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from the KDP's conservative, economically liberal profile, which favours markets over price controls.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the KDP's market-leaning, property-protecting profile.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred; the peshmerga are the movement's military form, and party youth wings are political rather than drilled national-service bodies.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred; Kurds have been targeted by chemical weapons and the movement wants no weapons of mass destruction in Kurdistan.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The Kurdistan Region hosts allied foreign forces for security and support against Baghdad, so adherents accept bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Recognition of the Anfal and other mass killings of Kurds as genocide is a central, widely pursued aim of Kurdish national politics.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The mainstream KDP/PUK movement is indifferent to this; its economic views are mixed.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from the peshmerga tradition and armed autonomy struggle, which accept lethal force.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Kurdish nationalists often trace the nation to ancient peoples such as the Medes, though scholars dispute continuity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred; the mainstream movement has no constructivist view of sex.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from the regional quota for women in parliament, which assumes women as a shared political group.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Fallen peshmerga and fighters in the autonomy struggle are honoured as martyrs (shehid) in public life.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred; the KDP is secular and treats politics as a contest over autonomy and interests.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The movement's aim is a unified Kurdistan gathering the Kurds, not a homeland serving a diaspora.

culture-before-state.rationale: The movement pursues autonomy and an independence referendum, putting statehood ahead of cultural revival.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred; the mainstream movement is secular and has no view on divine language.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred; the mainstream secular movement is not concerned with judging religious texts.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The Kurdistan Region reserves seats for minorities and keeps them in the economy; the claim of majority economic control is not a stated aim.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Nationalists claim disputed areas such as Kirkuk for the Kurdistan Region and want Kurdish-inhabited regions united.

independent-unions.rationale: Mainstream Kurdish nationalism has no labour doctrine; the market-leaning KDP and leftist currents would differ, so this is a genuine split inferred from the sources.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The movement is national rather than class-based, and its parties range from conservative to leftist, so adherents split on this.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred: the Kurdistan Region runs public hospitals and utilities, and nothing in the movement opposes this.

second-chamber.rationale: The movement has no doctrine on legislative structure; Kurdistan's own parliament is unicameral while Iraq's federal system includes a federal council, so adherents are not committed either way.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred: the KDP is economically liberal and favours private and national enterprise, and local-community ownership is a doctrine of the excluded confederalist strand.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred: confederal assembly-led rule is the excluded PKK-style strand's model; the mainstream seeks a state or federal autonomy with a government of its own.

family-wage.rationale: The movement has no wage doctrine and its parties span market-oriented to leftist, so adherents split.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Inferred at weak strength: nothing in the movement opposes faster approval, and regional governments generally favour modernising health services.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: The movement never addressed research funding, and no principle points either way.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Never addressed by the mainstream movement, and no core principle bears on it; KDP and PUK governments have not made financial privacy an issue.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred: Kurdish nationalists have faced state surveillance and repression in Turkey, Iran and Syria, which makes free expression under pseudonyms mildly congenial.

person-over-state.rationale: The movement stresses the nation's collective right to self-determination while its parties are liberal or conservative, so no clear stance on individual versus state emerges.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The KDP is secular while Islamic currents are excluded from this strand, and the nationalists are religiously mixed, so adherents split.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred: Kurdish nationalists want autonomy guaranteed in Iraq's constitution rather than revocable by Baghdad, and fear its withdrawal.

gm-crops.rationale: The movement never addressed agricultural biotechnology.

dense-cities.rationale: The movement never addressed urban form.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Kurdish nationalism is defined by the Kurds as a nation defined by language and heritage, not by race, and the sources show no racial doctrine.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in Kurdish ethnic identity, language and heritage is central, though it is framed as national rather than racial pride.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred: the movement's armed force, the peshmerga, is framed as defending the Kurdish homeland, and the movement seeks independence rather than conquest.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Kurdish nationalism treats the Kurds as one nation across four states, united by language and history despite state borders and dialect and religious differences.

communal-electorates.rationale: The mainstream KDP/PUK movement is secular and demands national self-rule, not sectarian representation, and the KRG reserves seats for minorities within common elections; inferred.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Kurds see the Sevres-to-Lausanne settlement as a great-power partition of Kurdistan, but the claim concerns outside division of their homeland more than a current plot to partition a state; inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: Kurdish nationalism has no tuition doctrine; adherents range from market-leaning KDP supporters to leftist currents.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental taxation is not an issue the movement addresses; its oil-dependent regional economy and split parties make it neutral.

future-generations.rationale: The movement has no stated doctrine on duties to future generations; adherents are split.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The strand is socially mixed: the KRG has a women's quota, but the conservative KDP holds no view on distinct female values.

arms-reduction.rationale: A stateless people defending itself with the peshmerga and seeking independence is inferred to oppose cutting arms to a minimum.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The movement cites treaties such as Sevres but has no stance on secrecy in diplomacy; its leaders negotiate privately with Baghdad and Ankara while appealing to public opinion.

capital-controls.rationale: The KDP's economically liberal, investment-seeking profile and the KRG's open oil and investment dealings imply opposition to capital controls; inferred.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The KDP and PUK rely on their own peshmerga forces, so mainstream Kurdish nationalists do not accept a state monopoly on arms where that state is hostile; inferred from their armed autonomy struggle.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: A movement fighting for a homeland through armed struggle against Turkey, Iraq, Iran and Syria would not tell soldiers to refuse; inferred from the peshmerga tradition.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Kurdish nationalist parties have no defined labour-relations programme; inferred as neutral.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax-credit policy is not addressed by the movement; inferred as neutral.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The KDP is economically liberal but fiscal rules are not an issue the movement addresses.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: As a stateless people disadvantaged by the post-1918 settlement, Kurdish nationalists would likely favour fairer international rules; inferred from the Sevres and Lausanne grievance.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The mainstream strand seeks to build or take over its own state institutions, such as the KRG, rather than destroy them; the PKK-style strand is excluded from scope.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The KDP's liberal profile and the PKK's confederalism pull in different directions; mainstream nationalists have no stated view on economic experimentation.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Environmental accounting is not a topic for the movement; inferred as neutral.

sacred-nation.rationale: Kurdish nationalism treats the Kurdish nation as a lasting community worth sacrifice, as in the martyr tradition, but the sources do not frame it as sacred; inferred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Student loans are not addressed by the movement; inferred as neutral.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Kurdish nationalists describe Kurdistan as a colonised territory divided and exploited by the four states, and cite Iraqi central control of oil revenue in the KRG dispute.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Kurdish nationalism claims universal rights of self-determination for peoples and language rights, which assumes common human dignity; inferred.

public-service-media.rationale: The movement has no stated policy on public broadcasting; Kurdish-language media are a language-rights demand rather than a public-media programme.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Kurdish nationalism has no doctrine on religious truth; its parties range from secular to Islamic and the Kurds include Muslims, Yazidis and others, so this is split.

farm-price-support.rationale: No farm doctrine is stated; mild support is inferred from the KRG's state-led, rural-rooted governance, which is why it is only low confidence.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Kurdish nationalism has no state of its own and no stated nuclear position, so no answer can be inferred from its aims.

workers-own-party.rationale: The mainstream KDP/PUK movement is a cross-class national front rather than a workers' party, so a separate class party is inferred to be unwanted.

ban-fgm.rationale: Mainstream parties favour modernising women's rights (the KRG has a women's quota), so a ban is inferred, not stated in the sources.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the movement's secular, modernising profile and the KRG's women's quota; equal land rights are not directly discussed.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Kurdish nationalists treat Kurmanji, Sorani and other varieties as one Kurdish language across four states, a unifying claim inferred from the language grievances in the sources.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Mainstream Kurdish parties are state-building and statist, so agency regulation is inferred over private suits; no pollution policy is stated.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Tribal leaders have mattered in the KDP's history but the movement's institutions are parliamentary; adherents are split and the sources do not address it.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The movement prioritises national and economic development, with oil central to its aims; this is inferred from the oil dispute rather than stated.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Kurdish nationalism has no stated criminal-sentencing doctrine, so adherents are inferred to be split.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The movement is mostly concerned with its own language rights; no position on immigrant language requirements is stated.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: No doctrine on union membership; the KDP is market-leaning and other currents are leftist, so adherents are split.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; adherents are split.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the secular, pluralist outlook of the mainstream parties and the region's mixed religious communities.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred from the KDP/PUK commitment to a parliamentary system and the 2017 referendum as an exercise in popular self-determination.

premarital-sex.rationale: No doctrine on personal morality; adherents range from conservative to secular.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the movement's own repression by states that cut communications; adherents are split.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from the Kurdistan Region's public-sector salaries and relief rather than market-style cash replacement.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from the Kurdistan Region's parliamentary quota for women and the movement's support for women's political rights.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from the mainstream movement's secular but not anti-religious stance; religion is not blamed as a main cause.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the movement's claim of a Kurdish nation defined by language and history, not by race.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from the Kurdistan Region's state bodies for women's affairs.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Mainstream Kurdish nationalism has no doctrine on first-claim property; its parties span market-leaning and leftist views, inferred.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Kurdish nationalists seek recognition of Anfal and Halabja as atrocities against Kurds and would welcome international justice; inferred.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The mainstream movement is secular-national and not bound to a literal scriptural doctrine, though a Kurdish-Islamic current exists; inferred.

gendered-self-government.rationale: The Kurdistan Region has parliamentary quotas for women, suggesting mainstream support for gender guarantees in self-rule; inferred.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The mainstream KDP-led movement is conservative and market-leaning and has no stake in defending planned economies; inferred.

indirect-election.rationale: The movement stresses popular votes such as regional elections and the 2017 referendum, so direct election is the likely preference; inferred.

national-church-status.rationale: The movement is ethnic-national and religiously mixed, with no national church to privilege; inferred.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Autonomy for Kurdish-majority areas is the movement's core demand and is realised in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Kurdish nationalists demand a vote on disputed areas such as Kirkuk and put independence to a referendum in 2017.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: The movement rejects the post-First World War borders that split the Kurds among four states and points to the Sevres promise of Kurdistan.

simple-living.rationale: Nationalism makes no claim about personal frugality; inferred.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Kurdish nationalists oppose Arabization of Kirkuk and other Kurdish-majority areas, so limits on outside settlement are inferred as welcome.

equal-conscription.rationale: The movement has no stated line on conscription, and Peshmerga service and mixed practice leave adherents split; inferred.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Kurdish nationalism rests on a claim to a divided homeland, Kurdistan, and a duty to defend it.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The KDP programme is secular, liberal and constitutional; killing without trial is not part of it, so inferred.

close-ties-china.rationale: Relations with China are not addressed by the movement; inferred as neutral.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The movement is pan-Kurdish and the KDP and others have supported Kurds in neighbouring states.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The KDP is described as economically liberal and market-leaning, so common ownership with compensation is inferred as unlikely.

self-ownership.rationale: The KDP's liberal profile supports individual rights, though the sources do not discuss self-ownership; inferred.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Tax design is not discussed in the sources; inferred as neutral.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Welfare design is not addressed in the sources; inferred as neutral.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The Kurdistan Region operates through parties, a parliament and a government, so bypassing parties is inferred as contrary.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The KDP profile is conservative and market-leaning, but no source speaks to business privileges; inferred and split.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The KDP is described as secular, supporting politics not organised by denomination; inferred.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The movement has no stated position on ancestral values versus technology; inferred as neutral.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The Kurdistan Region has a women's quota and a secular leadership; inferred support for women's divorce rights.

national-resource-control.rationale: Control of Kurdistan's oil against Baghdad is a central dispute of the autonomy struggle.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred from the market-leaning KDP and the Kurdistan Region's open investment policy, which treat fairness as a matter of process.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred: the Kurdistan Region relies on oil revenue and foreign investment, and a financial tax is not a nationalist demand.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Nationalists stress the Kurds' division between states, not a racism-versus-other-factors debate, so the answer is inferred and neutral.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Adherents are split: unjust state laws are resisted as imposed by occupying states, yet the movement also seeks recognised legal autonomy.

automate-paid-work.rationale: The movement has no position on automation; mainstream parties are not centred on it.

multipolar-world.rationale: Kurdish nationalists want a Kurdish state or autonomy within a stable order; the movement has no stated view on global power distribution.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Not an issue for the mainstream movement; leftist currents hold it but the KDP and PUK strands do not.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred: national feeling is central, and the leftist currents combine it with social solidarity, while the market-leaning KDP does not oppose it.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred from the movement's centring of national and cultural-language identity as the main political cause.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The mainstream movement rejects single-party communist rule and the nation-state-rejecting strand is excluded from this scope, so this is inferred.

missingStatements.text: The Kurdish people should be allowed to unite in an independent state of their own.
missingStatements.rationale: Independent Kurdistan was demanded at Paris in 1919, offered conditionally at Sevres and put to vote in 2017.

missingStatements.text: A people deprived of its own language in schools and public life has the right to teach and use it officially.
missingStatements.rationale: Bans on Kurdish in Turkey, Syria and Iran are a core grievance and Kurdish is official in Iraq.

notes: The PKK-descended democratic confederalist strand and the Kurdish-Islamic strand would answer differently on state, religion and economy. Kurds in Iran and Syria mostly seek autonomy or federalism rather than independence.
